cases.note: §7.6 crossing §17. The robot resolves its own ceilings and guard partition and until this field existed nothing carried them: §32.1 asks a device page for exactly this and the Hub’s own route answered with a `gaps` list naming it. Frozen because the two halves of the sentence an operator reads — which guards run, and whether anything enforces them — are in different fields, and an edition that agreed about one could disagree about the other.

cases.note: Two pending actions declared out of order, which no case had. `blocking` was sorted from the first day and `pending` is a **second** list of the same facts, sorted separately — so an edition emitting it in declaration order agreed about every claim in this corpus and disagreed about the bytes of every check-in carrying more than one action. The reason it has to be sorted rather than merely stable: §34.4 collapses check-ins, and two documents that differ only in the order of a list are two documents a queue cannot tell are duplicates.

cases.note: §10’s contradiction: a measure that says `unmeasured` and carries a digest anyway. Both fields are well-typed and no case had ever put them together, which left the whole question of what a consumer sees unpinned. The digest is **dropped**, and the reason is the query it would otherwise answer: §32.1 puts a fleet column on "which robots are running image `sha256:…`", and a robot whose slot was never read must not appear in that answer. The sentence already says `an unmeasured OS image`; a digest beside it would be the same report contradicting itself in the machine-readable half, where nobody is reading English to catch it.
